hz_coal_air.description:
I'm Vesna Orlova. I taught palaeobotany in Perm, before. I've been down here since the ground opened under Walt's basin, a year after the Integration, and I still don't know how this place can exist.

This is the Carboniferous. Three hundred million years ago, before there were flowers, when the air had so much oxygen in it that insects grew to the size of dogs. Those are griffinflies over the water, and those things in the ferns are worse. They've found my camp. Kill enough of the flies and the stalkers that I can get back to work.

hz_coal_green.accept_text: The thousand-leg is in the coal seam, north-west. The grove is at the very north, so go together.
hz_coal_green.turn_in_text:
The air's thinner already. Can you feel it?

The forest won't die. It'll just stop pushing. It'll go back to being what it should be, a place that's hard to find and harder to leave. I think I'll stay a while longer. Take something, because you earned it.

hz_lanternmere_lamplighter.description:
There used to be a man who kept the lanterns on the causeway, so travellers wouldn't wander into the water. When he died, he kept doing it, except now he lights them to lead people in. Every wisp on the mere is one of his lamps.

The Amani Barrow-Shades guard the top of the causeway for him. Take them down, and then him, and take friends. He's had a long time to get good at it.

hz_lanternmere_lights.description:
I'm Sami Halonen. I studied peat bogs in Finland for twenty years, back home, and I've never seen one like this. The plague went all the way round it and never came in.

But the lights did. Every Mere Wisp out there drifts over the water at dusk, and whoever follows one walks into the mere and comes back up a Fen Drowned. I've lost two travellers that way this month. Put the lights out, and the drowned with them.
hz_lanternmere_lights.turn_in_text:
That's much quieter. Back home we called them will-o'-the-wisps and said they were marsh gas. These aren't marsh gas.

I'd like to know what they are, if you'll help me catch some.

hz_springs_beads.description:
The pools are wrong. They were always hot, but since the Integration they're hotter than any spring I ever logged, and the colours have started moving outward a little every week.

The steam things and the mud things carry beads of sinter in them, set from the same water. Bring me a handful and I'll work out how hot the water runs below and how fast it's rising.

hz_springs_bull.description:
There's one more thing, and I've been putting it off.

The herd bull. He was old when he came through, and the heat in this place has got into him. He doesn't lead the herd any more, he goes through it, calves and all. I've watched it for a month hoping he'd settle, and he won't.

I can't do it myself. I tried, and I couldn't make my hands work. Make it quick.

hz_springs_clockwork.accept_text: The cone at the north end of the basin. You'll hear it before you see it, so bring friends.
hz_springs_clockwork.turn_in_text:
It's quiet, for the first time in three years.

The pools will cool now, slowly. The colours will come back in from the edges, the way they used to.

hz_springs_herd.description:
I'm Walt Dempsey. I was a ranger at Yellowstone for thirty-one years, and three years ago a piece of it came through with me. Not the whole park. This basin, the herd, the pools, and me.

The wolves and the bears came too, and that's fine, that's how it's meant to work. But they've got nowhere to roam in here, so they're taking calves faster than the herd can drop them. Thin out the wolves and the grizzlies in the burnt timber before there's no herd left to protect.

hz_sunward_breach.turn_in_text:
It's really dead? The breach is quiet. I can hear birds at the north end, for the first time in years.

The ward can heal now, if the Magister lets it. That's the next problem, and it's the one I've been dreading.

hz_sunward_shards.turn_in_text:
It's got weeks, maybe less. The Magister's pouring everything he has into it, and it's eating him alive.

And something on the other side is chewing at the breach. I can hear it at night.

hz_winter_ice.turn_in_text:
It's stopped moving. I put a stake in the snow at its edge this morning and it hasn't moved since.

The winter will go on in here, the way it should. It just won't come any further. Thank you, truly.

hz_winter_ochre.turn_in_text:
It's the same. It's exactly the same.

Someone stood here twenty thousand years ago and painted a lion. The lion's still in there, by the way. I'd stay out of the cave if I were you, or not.

hz_winter_wolves.description:
My name's Ana Vukovic. I was a palaeontologist in Zagreb, back home, and I spent my life digging up the bones of everything you can see out there. Woolly mammoths, cave bears, lions, they all died out on Earth before anyone learned to write, and here they are, breathing.

This is the last ice age, a piece of it, and it came through the Integration whole. But it's a small piece, and the dire wolves and the cave bears are eating it faster than it can feed them. Thin them out, please, before there's nothing left to study.
